nodes.name: Fe2O3-NiOxHy/NF hydrothermal synthesis
nodes.procedure: Certain amounts of Fe(NO3)3·9H2O (4 mM) and Na4EDTA·xH2O (2 mM) were dissolved into 50 ml of DI water to afford a homogeneous aqueous solution, followed by adding 25 ml of methanol into it. The mixed solution obtained above was then transferred into a Teflon-lined container containing NF substrates and enclosed into a 100-ml stainless steel autoclave followed by heating at 190°C for 3 hours. After the hydrothermal process, the as-obtained Fe2O3-NiOxHy/NF products were washed with DI water several times to remove possible chemical impurities and dried in oven at 75°C. To characterize the physicochemical properties of ultrasmall Fe2O3 NPs, the red precipitates (mainly Fe2O3) yielded from the above hydrothermal process were further collected and washed with DI water several times, followed by drying in oven at 75°C.

nodes.procedure: 50 ml of aqueous solution containing 5 mM Ni(NO3)2 and 2.5 mM Na4EDTA·xH2O was prepared and enclosed into a Teflon-lined autoclave container with PTF substrates. nodes.description: OER performance comparison in 1 M KOH (NF substrates)
nodes.source_text: The electrochemical OER performances of the electrodes prepared were first evaluated in a purified 1 M KOH solution at a scan rate of 1 mV s⁻¹. As shown in Fig. 2A, Fe₂O₃ - NiOₓHᵧ / NF exhibits the earliest onset potential [∼ 1.42 V versus reversible hydrogen electrode (RHE)] among the three electrodes tested, and only requires an overpotential of 290 mV to reach a current density (j) of 100 mA cm⁻² without any iR correction... the NiOₓHᵧ / NF and pure NF electrodes call for additional 130 and 220 mV of overpotential
no obvious decay of OER activity can be observed on Fe₂O₃ - NiOₓHᵧ / NF after over 50 hours durability test

nodes.characterization_summary: SEM reveals highly rippled and interconnected nanosheet structure on nickel foam.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Scanning electron microscopy (SEM) analysis revealed that the hydrothermal process has resulted in the formation of a highly rippled and interconnected nanosheet structure on the surface of the NF skeleton (Fig. 1A and fig. S2).

nodes.characterization_summary: TEM shows thin nanosheet structure decorated with ultrafine nanoparticles between 5 and 10 nm.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Transmission electron microscopy (TEM) images (Fig. 1B and fig. S3) showed that the electrocatalyst produced through the as-prepared method is composed of a thin nanosheet structure decorated with numerous ultrafine NPs (between 5 and 10 nm).

nodes.characterization_summary: HAADF-STEM shows hexagonal structure of ultrafine Fe₂O₃ NPs with lattice fringes of 0.27 nm corresponding to (104) planes of hematite.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The clear lattice fringes of approximately 0.27 nm on the NPs (Fig. 1C) provide additional evidence for the highly crystalline structure of the NPs. These fringes can be assigned to the ⟨104⟩ planes of a hematite structure.

nodes.characterization_summary: EDS maps show spatially separated distribution of Ni and Fe elements with Fe concentrated on NPs and Ni throughout the nanosheet structure.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Upon further analysis of the HAADF-STEM image and the corresponding energy-dispersive x-ray spectroscopy (EDS) maps (Fig. 1, D to G, and fig. S4) from a selected area of Fe₂O₃-NiOₓHᵧ, it was observed that there is a spatially separated distribution of Ni and Fe elements across the composite.

nodes.characterization_summary: EELS confirms absence of Fe signals in nanosheet area, indicating nanosheets are predominantly NiOₓHᵧ rather than NiFeOₓHᵧ.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Notably, the electron energy-loss spectroscopy (EELS) measurements (fig. S5) have further provided evidence of the absence of Fe signals in the nanosheet area, suggesting that the nanosheet is predominantly composed of NiOₓHᵧ, rather than NiFeOₓHᵧ.

nodes.characterization_summary: AFM reveals average thickness of 1 nm for iron oxide NPs.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Furthermore, through the atomic force microscopy characterization (fig. S6), an average thickness of 1 nm was revealed for the iron oxide NPs.

nodes.characterization_summary: XPS shows Ni 2p spectra dominated by Ni²⁺ with Ni 2p₃/₂ peak shifting positively to higher binding energy, indicating strong electronic interaction between NiOₓHᵧ and Fe₂O₃.
nodes.evidence_snippet: It was revealed that the formation of ultrasmall Fe₂O₃ NPs on the NiOₓHᵧ nanosheet does not disturb the valence state of Ni species, exhibiting the similar Ni 2p spectra on both NiOₓHᵧ/NF and Fe₂O₃-NiOₓHᵧ/NF that are dominated by Ni²⁺ (Fig. 1H).

nodes.characterization_summary: Fe K-edge XANES shows main absorption edge at ≈7133.8 eV, decreased main absorption peak intensity, higher pre-edge intensity, and shift to low energy side (~0.4 eV) compared to bulk Fe₂O₃, indicating electron-rich Fe₂O₃ phase with lower local oxygen coordination (average coordination number 3.4).
nodes.evidence_snippet: As shown in Fig. 1I, the Fe K-edge x-ray absorption near-edge spectra (XANES) features a main absorption edge at ≈7133.8 eV... This not only indicates a lower local oxygen coordination of Fe atoms but also further evidences an electron-rich Fe₂O₃ phase in Fe₂O₃-NiOₓHᵧ catalysts.
